The coaching adjustment-detection system operates as a cascading hierarchy of dual-purpose operators. The unsupervised regime-shift detector (Task Embedding Drift) identifies changes in underlying behavior, while the changepoint trigger provides actionable timing. Regime-specific aggression measurement calibrates the direction and magnitude of adaptation, and governance ensures that responses are appropriately scaled to avoid overfitting. Together, these four primitives form a closed-loop control system where detection leads to estimation, which informs policy, which is vetted through cross-layer consistency checks.
